title.narrative: Advocacy on Human Rights Legislation in the Philippines

description.narrative:
This project aims to strengthen the capacity and solidarity of human rights defenders (HRDs) to promote a human rights-based approach in national and local legislation in the Philippines. Despite the country’s strong constitutional foundation and a legacy of civil society–driven human rights laws, current political conditions reflect a marked slowdown in legislative action on key human rights concerns. These include the protection of human rights defenders, criminalization of extrajudicial killings, ratification of the International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance (ICPPED), and re-ratification of the Rome Statute.
Building on decades of grassroots and policy-level advocacy, the project is led by KARAPATAN, a long-standing human rights alliance in the Philippines. It addresses the urgent need to equip HRDs with the necessary tools, knowledge, and platforms to advocate for new legislation and ensure that existing legal standards align with international human rights obligations.
Core activities include two training workshops for HRDs, preceded by preparatory meetings to design the training modules and evaluation tools. The workshops will focus on advocacy skills and include writeshops for developing concrete legislative proposals and campaign materials. Participants will be selected to ensure diversity, gender balance, and intergenerational representation. To build momentum around legislative advocacy, the project will also conduct two roundtable discussions each with national and local legislators, at least four meetings between HRDs and lawmakers, and two public forums to promote the human rights legislative agenda.
By the end of the project, HRDs will be better equipped to engage with lawmakers, and there will be increased dialogue and public awareness around key human rights issues. Direct beneficiaries include the trained HRDs and legislators engaged, while the broader public and civil society organizations will benefit from improved policy discourse and legal protections. Through this initiative, KARAPATAN aims to help revive momentum for rights-based lawmaking and strengthen civil society’s role in shaping democratic governance in the Philippines.
The project aims to train human rights defenders in effective advocacy through inclusive and gender-balanced workshops. It also targets engagement with national and local legislators through roundtable discussions, advocacy meetings, and public forums. A strong Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) component will ensure continuous assessment and improvement, culminating in a final report by December 2026.
